issues.legal_issue: A mineral lease deemed to have been granted by the State after the relevant cutoff is a new lease and cannot be modified under rules governing existing mining leases.
material_facts: The original head lease was granted before the relevant cutoff and remained in force when the estate vested in the State.
On vesting, the original lessor’s interests ended, and the mining rights were deemed leased by the State to the holder of the subsisting lease for the remainder of its term.
The Controller modified the head lease and its sub-leases under rules applicable to existing mining leases.
The Supreme Court treated the statutory lease and the sub-leases as new leases granted after the cutoff.
issues.conclusion: The statutory lease was not an existing mining lease within the meaning of the applicable rules, so the Controller lacked jurisdiction to modify it; the sub-leases could not be modified on that basis either.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10 of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, a subsisting mining lease was deemed leased by the State to its holder from the date of vesting. The Court held that this created a new lease after the relevant cutoff, rather than continuing an existing lease. Rule 2(c) of the Mining Leases (Modification of Terms) Rules, 1956 limited the relevant category of existing leases by reference to that cutoff, and rule 6 authorized modification only of leases within that category. The Court also relied on section 10’s treatment of the sub-leases following the end of the original lessor’s interests. No earlier cases were relied on for this holding.

rule.if: lease_modification_appeal and pre_cutoff_lease_subsisted and lessor_interest_ended_on_vesting and state_lease_arose_after_cutoff

predicates.lease_modification_appeal: A party challenged an order modifying a mining lease under rules for modifying existing leases.
predicates.pre_cutoff_lease_subsisted: The mining lease was created before the relevant cutoff and remained in force when the property interest vested.
predicates.lessor_interest_ended_on_vesting: The original lessor’s interest ended when the property interest vested in the State.
predicates.state_lease_arose_after_cutoff: The law deemed the State to have leased the mining property to the holder after the relevant cutoff.
predicates.controller_lacked_authority_to_modify_le: The authority that issued the modification order had no power under the existing-lease rules to modify the lease.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns an order modifying a mining lease, and a pre-cutoff lease subsisted until vesting that ended the original lessor’s interest and gave rise to a State lease after the cutoff, the authority lacked power to modify that lease under rules governing existing leases.
